scope: Locally authored fictional Markdown, HTML, and programmatically constructed DOCX cases. These are not application-origin captures, real user documents, device tests, or compatibility evidence.

cases.reason: CJK source text must survive all article exports.
Right-to-left text must survive without script or direction stripping.
Combining marks and precomposed accents should retain the input characters.
Supplementary-plane emoji and variation selectors should survive the Word ZIP.
Ordinary punctuation should not be reinterpreted as article metadata.
Separate ordinary paragraphs need both text passages and stable export ordering.
Opening H1 moves into a separate title while the remaining body survives.
Common inline emphasis must not delete text during three-format export.
Supported strikethrough must survive as an actual mark in HTML and Word.
The link label and exact safe HTTPS target should survive both HTML exports.
Bullet item identity should remain across destination formats.
A numbered list starting at four should retain its items and numbering structure.
A nested mixed list should retain child text instead of flattening it away.
A simple header table should preserve cell rows across HTML and Word.
Fenced code should retain literal text while remaining inert.
Literal source tags inside inline code must remain text, never active DOM.
A normal Markdown quote should retain its content in the destination.
An unfinished front-matter block must reject before replacing current writing.
Duplicate metadata fields must reject without choosing an arbitrary title.
Control bytes must reject before a dangerous or lossy export.
Reserved metadata names must not reach object properties or the writer's article.
Unsafe slug values must reject rather than being silently rewritten.
